evidence: src/domain/services/StockManager.ts: class StockManager has only stock-related methods: canReserveStock, reserveStock and releaseStock.
src/domain/services/StockManager.ts: canReserveStock calls product.canReserve(line.quantity) and does not re-implement the stock check, so the rule stays in Product.
src/domain/services/StockManager.ts: reserveStock calls product.reserve and releaseStock calls product.release, so state changes go through the entity's own methods.
src/domain/services/StockManager.ts: the same product lookup (`products.find(p => p.id === line.productId)`) is repeated in all three methods. It is a small repeated helper step, not a copied rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has one file, src/domain/services/StockManager.ts, and it covers a single concern: reserving and releasing stock for an order. All three methods leave the stock rules to the Product entity (canReserve, reserve, release) and do not re-implement them, so each rule stays in one place and the entity abstraction is used consistently. The lookup `products.find(p => p.id === line.productId)` appears in all three methods. That is a small repeated mechanical step, not a copied business rule. reserveStock and releaseStock also skip missing products without reporting it, while canReserveStock returns false for a missing product. This is a robustness point and not a broken boundary. Neither issue meets the rubric's fail criteria.
